title: Introduce sequence-length bucketing and runtime padding minimizer for dynamic batching
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Dynamic batching in the serving runtime can suffer from token padding overhead when requests with widely varying sequence lengths are grouped. This PR implements a lightweight sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimizer heuristic in the scheduler to reduce wasted computation while preserving throughput and tail latency SLOs. Design summary: 1) Client request seq_len metadata is captured at ingress and used as a primary key for slotting into short-lived buckets. 2) Buckets are organized into exponential bins (1-8, 9-16, 17-32, 33-64, 65-128, 129+), with runtime-configurable max bucket lifetime and max bucket fill thresholds. 3) A padding cost model estimates per-batch wasted tokens; the scheduler uses a utility function (throughput_gain - padding_cost - wait_penalty) to decide whether to flush a bucket or wait for more similar-length requests. 4) To avoid harmful interactions with KV cache warm paths, the heuristic keeps cached and non-cached requests separate by default and merges them only if the estimated cost is favorable. 5) Continuous-batching compatibility: when traffic is homogeneous or under high QPS, the heuristic gracefully degrades to existing continuous batching logic. 6) Telemetry and knobs: new metrics (bucket_fill_rate, avg_padding_ratio, bucket_flush_reasons) and two config flags (seqlen_bucketing_enabled, padding_cost_alpha) exposed via the runtime flags and Console. Implementation highlights: - scheduler/queue_manager: new bucket index and flush decision path; added fast path for small-seq hot requests. - runtime/kernel_allocator: minor adjustments to ensure kernel launch shapes match bucketed sequence lengths; no new kernels introduced. - kvcache/integration: added tagging to preserve cache hit accounting when separating request streams. - perf/benchmarks: added a microbench harness that feeds realistic seqlen distributions and measures p50/p95 token latency and token-efficiency. Rollout plan: staged canary in Dedicated region us-west-2 with 10% of traffic; metrics validated over 48-hour window (latency, throughput, cost per token). If regressions exceed 2x p99 latency or revenue-weighted token-cost increases by >5%, the feature auto-rolls back. Backwards compatibility: flags default off; safe to enable per-deployment. Related work: complements earlier batching improvements in ENG-3901 and the padding-aware batching prototype in a private branch.

file_snippets: runtime/scheduler/bucketing_policy.h: class BucketingPolicy { public: size_t bin_for_len(size_t len) const; double estimate_padding_cost(const Batch&); bool should_flush(Bucket&); };

runtime/scheduler/queue_manager.cc: if (seqlen_bucketing_enabled) { auto bin = policy.bin_for_len(req.seq_len); buckets[bin].push(req); if (policy.should_flush(buckets[bin])) flush_bucket(bin); } else enqueue_continuous(req);
perf_summary: Canary results: p50 token latency improved by 6.4% for mixed workloads, p95 improved 4.1%. Token-efficiency (useful_tokens / allocated_tokens) improved from 0.72 to 0.81 on mixed-length traces. For extremely skewed short-request workloads there is a small 1-2% throughput regression due to extra bucket bookkeeping; opt-in knob allows bypass. End-to-end cost-per-inference decreased by ~3.7% in our dedicated canary experiments.

review_comments: Evan Chu: Please add a short note explaining why exponential bins were chosen over linear bins. Also add a safety check to avoid unbounded bucket memory usage.
Author (Priya): Exponential bins provide better handling of heavy-tail length distributions we see in prod; added bucket cap and LRU eviction for long-lived bins. See commit c6a7b21.
María Gonzales: We should validate that separating cached/non-cached streams doesn't cause cache accounting drift. Are you exposing metrics to detect regressions?
Author (Priya): Added cache-tagging and metrics bucket_cache_hit_ratio; integration tests added to assert accounting parity in steady state.
Liam O'Connor: Could we add a conservative default alpha for padding_cost to avoid aggressive waiting?
Author (Priya): Default padding_cost_alpha set to 0.6; knob exposed and documented.
notes_for_ops: Enable seqlen_bucketing_enabled=false by default. Gradually enable in Canary with runtime flag.
Watch metrics: bucket_fill_rate, avg_padding_ratio, bucket_flush_reasons, bucket_cache_hit_ratio
If p99 latency regresses >2x or token-cost rises >5%, flip flag and open incident runbook ENG-4128-rollback
release_notes: Introduce sequence-length bucketing in the runtime scheduler to reduce padding overhead and improve token-efficiency on mixed-length workloads; exposed runtime flags and telemetry for safe rollout; no customer-facing API changes.
